decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed “paste a link, it’s stored with a title.” Round 1 client said the proposed scope worked and approved planning.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Saving a bookmark by entering a URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker specified “Auto-fetch page titles best-effort; fall back to the URL,” without description, favicon, or preview-image collection. Round 1 client broadly approved the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Title-only collection omits three required metadata fields; broad approval does not express or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker separated URL-only saving from the later P3 ability to “fix titles,” presenting no title/description editing before save. Round 1 client broadly approved.
decisions.note: Specification gate. The proposal supports later title editing but not editing collected title/description both before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker defined editing as “fix titles, update tags,” while the reference also requires URL, description, and note editing. Round 1 client said the proposed scope worked.
decisions.note: Specification gate. The explicitly limited edit-field set diverges; the response did not identify the omitted fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed “click to open the page.” Round 1 client approved the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Opening the original bookmark target conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed adding tags and filtering by tag. Round 1 client approved the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Tag assignment and filtering to a selected tag conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker fixed browsing to “see your list newest-first,” rather than offering selectable sort keys. Round 1 client broadly approved.
decisions.note: Specification gate. A fixed newest-first order does not provide user-selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed removing bookmarks with confirmation. Round 1 client approved the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate. Permanent bookmark deletion conforms; confirmation is an orthogonal safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly placed “importing browser bookmarks” out of scope for v1. Round 1 client said “The proposed scope and priorities work for me.”
decisions.note: Specification gate. Browser-bookmark import was explicitly excluded. The client did not state the reference expectation or specifically accept its absence, so the broad approval is not accepted_divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker said only “search by keyword”; Round 3 listed “Search” and Round 4 “live search.” Client responses approved each gate but never established searched fields, case handling, #tag syntax, Boolean/parenthesized expressions, or exact phrases.
decisions.note: Linked specification-to-implementation decision. Search exists, but the presentations do not establish whether its semantics conform or diverge; generic approval does not resolve the missing evidence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed “notes”; Round 3 said “Tags/notes on create”; Round 4 mentioned “long-note truncation.” No presentation or client response establishes Markdown authoring and rendered viewing.
decisions.note: Linked specification-to-implementation decision. Note support is recorded, but Markdown behavior cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed seeing a bookmark list; Round 4 described a main view with bookmarks, tags, and notes. Neither the presentations nor client responses establish whether every item exposes title, description, tags, and favicon.
decisions.note: Linked specification-to-implementation decision. List existence is clear, but the required per-item fields and readability-first presentation cannot be fully established.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker’s plan again specified only “Titles auto-fetched best-effort,” with URL fallback. Round 2 client approved the plan without discussing missing metadata.
decisions.note: Planning gate. The design retained title-only metadata collection and omitted description, favicon, and preview image.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker proposed normalized-URL duplicate detection; Round 3 clarified the criterion as “same URL twice → warned, not duplicated.” Round 3 client approved full implementation without addressing edit guidance.
decisions.note: Linked plan/task decision. Warning and preventing duplication do not guide the user into editing the existing bookmark. The Round 3 clarification supplies the disposition, so the earlier ambiguity is not double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker planned normalized tag storage “so filtering by a tag and listing all tags is clean and fast.” Round 2 client approved.
decisions.note: Planning gate. The tag model supports assignment and selected-tag filtering.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker’s save phase listed “title fetch” but no description, favicon, or preview-image collection. Round 3 client authorized implementation.
decisions.note: Task gate. The actionable save tasks retained the incomplete metadata scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specified an add form and the test “add a valid link → appears with title.” Round 3 client authorized implementation.
decisions.note: Task gate. URL-based bookmark creation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker included “open-in-new-tab” in the browse phase. Round 3 client authorized implementation.
decisions.note: Task gate. Opening the original URL in a new tab is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker included “Tags/notes on create” and “tag filter.” Round 3 client authorized implementation.
decisions.note: Task gate. Tag assignment during creation and selected-tag filtering conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker listed tag creation, a tag filter, and GET /api/tags; Round 4 listed a tag filter. Neither presentation nor client response says whether existing tags are offered as entry autocomplete.
decisions.note: Linked task-to-implementation decision. The tag API could support autocomplete, but execution of that behavior cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker’s browse tasks again specified “newest-first,” with no selectable sort. Round 3 client authorized full implementation.
decisions.note: Task gate. The task breakdown operationalized a fixed order rather than user-selectable sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker included DELETE, delete UI, and confirmation. Round 3 client authorized implementation.
decisions.note: Task gate. Bookmark deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported a dedicated title-fetch component—“best-effort <title> fetch with URL fallback”—but no description, favicon, or preview-image collection. Round 4 client accepted the application.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The reported implementation retained title-only metadata; final acceptance did not surface that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker told the client that saving the same address twice “is warned rather than silently duplicated.” Round 4 client accepted the application without mentioning duplicate-edit behavior.
decisions.note: Implementation review. A warning is not the required guidance into editing the existing item, and generic final acceptance is not explicit acceptance of that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported a separate add form and edit dialog and said the app was built strictly to the approved specification, whose Round 1 behavior allowed title fixes only later. Round 4 client accepted the application without discussing pre-save editing.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The presentation carries forward after-save editing without the required before-save title/description editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported an edit dialog built “strictly against the approved spec”; the approved Round 1 edit scope was “fix titles, update tags.” Round 4 client said only that they could “edit” bookmarks and accepted the app.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The implemented edit decision inherits the restricted field set; the client did not identify the missing URL, description, and note editing requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker said all Round 3 tasks were complete and the app was built strictly against them; those tasks fixed the list to newest-first. Round 4 client accepted the application without mentioning sorting.
decisions.note: Implementation review. The completed task design provides no selectable sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported a working add form and invited the client to add a URL. Round 4 client confirmed “I can save” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation review. URL-based saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported “open-in-new-tab”; Round 4 client confirmed they could “reopen my bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation review. Navigation to the original URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported tags and a tag filter and invited immediate filtering by tag. Round 4 client confirmed they could “organize” bookmarks.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Tag assignment and selected-tag filtering conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker reported delete-with-confirmation and invited deletion of sample entries. Round 4 client confirmed “I can … delete” and accepted the app.
decisions.note: Implementation review. Permanent deletion conforms.

decision.evidence: Round 1 maker offered “A — Single-user, no login” or “B — Multi-user with accounts.” Round 1 client explicitly selected “Q1: A — single-user, no login.”
decision.note: Specification gate. The offered alternatives differed from the reference’s single-user scope; the client selected the reference-conforming alternative.
